text:
ani: FYI I prototyped a thin-index mode for safetensors that keeps only per-shard 'priority hints' in memory so we can avoid eagerly mapping entire index for huge checkpoints.
leo: interesting. is that the "index-light" idea from the RFC or something different?
ani: related, but simpler. we store a tiny header per shard: byte ranges, preferred load order, and a hotness score updated by runtime. not storing full offsets list.
pav: how do we serve range reads then? need offsets to do correct byte ranges for tensors.
ani: we still keep minimal offsets for big tensors that cross pages. small tensors use a fallback single-range read + memcopy. goal is to reduce metadata footprint and mmap churn.
claire: sounds promising for multi-GB models. failure modes? corrupt header or mismatch with actual shard layout on disk?
ani: we include a compact checksum (xxh64) per header and a manifest-level epoch. loader will verify and fall back to full index if checksum mismatch.
leo: what about warmup ordering? can we use the hotness score to drive progressive hydration: most likely-first, lazy rest.
pav: yes, but need admission control otherwise aggressive hydration from many requests can still flush the cache. we spoke about pool-level warmup budgets last week.
claire: also need manifest schema change to allow per-shard hint fields. ops should be able to generate them at upload time.
ani: prototype manifest snippet:

```
manifest_version: 2
shards:
  - id: s0
    url: s3://.../model.safetensors.part0
    hints:
      order: ["embeddings.weight","transformer.h.0.*"]
      hotness: 0.78
      checksum: "xxh64:abcd1234"
```

leo: that works. Storage will need a tool to bake hints; we can compute hotness from eval traces or prefix frequency and store it at bundle creation.
pav: migration path? we should support manifest-v2 alongside v1. loader should accept v1 and build hints lazily by sampling the index on first load.
ani: agreed. lazy-build of hints + cache them in local metadata store. avoid blocking serve path: lazy builder runs with low priority.
claire: telemetry we should emit: hint_build_time, hint_checksum_failures, "partial_stream_reads", and per-shard fallback_count.
leo: edge-case: transformers with many small tensors in many files -> too many small reads. consider a read-coalescer that merges adjacent requests into a single ranged read.
pav: we already have a coalescer prototype in weight-reader; needs tuning for SAFETENSOR framing.
bootstrap-bot: note: weight-bundle/uploader/pr-198 applied manifest_v2 schema validation to staging.
ani: next steps: 1) add manifest_v2 parser + fallback in loader 2) implement hint builder as async background job 3) add tests for mismatch fallback 4) instrument metrics. I'll open a PR for the loader changes.
claire: please include a small canary plan: enable on 1% of traffic, watch partial_stream_reads and fallback_count for 1 hour.
leo: and add a kill-switch flag to disable hint use per-pool.
pav: timeline: sounds good. ping me when PR is ready and I'll wire the coalescer integration.
ani: thanks. opening PR tonight.
